name: Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Disorder Due to a Large-Scale Single Deletion of Mitochondrial DNA

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Single Large-Scale mtDNA Deletion Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic clinical features such as progressive external ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, and muscle weakness
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficient fibers
Detection of a large-scale single deletion in mitochondrial DNA by molecular genetic testing
Elevated blood or cerebrospinal fluid lactate levels
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia or brainstem abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus confirmation of a large-scale single mtDNA deletion by genetic testing or muscle biopsy findings consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and molecular genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Bilateral, symmetric limitation of eye movements
Drooping of one or both eyelids

searchTerms: ragged red fibers seen in muscle biopsy
abnormal muscle fibers with ragged red appearance
muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
weakness in muscles near the trunk
weakness in upper arms and thighs

common.notes: Reduced ability to sustain physical activity

searchTerms: hearing loss from inner ear or nerve damage
abnormal heart rhythm due to conduction defects

occasional.notes: Difficulty swallowing due to muscle weakness
Mild to moderate deficits in executive function

rare.notes: Transient focal neurological deficits mimicking stroke

laboratory: Elevated blood and cerebrospinal fluid lactate and pyruvate levels
Increased serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia hyperintensities or brainstem abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating selective muscle involvement
genetic: Detection of a single large-scale deletion in mitochondrial DNA via Southern blot, long-range PCR, or next-generation sequencing
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX-deficient fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Cardiac conduction defects with heart block
Isolated progressive external ophthalmoplegia without multisystem involvement
Absence of large-scale mtDNA deletions in some cases

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia with ptosis
Elevated lactate levels in blood or CSF
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX deficiency
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Gorman GS, Schaefer AM, Ng Y, et al. Prevalence of nuclear and mitochondrial DNA mutations related to adult mitochondrial disease. Ann Neurol. 2015 May;77(5):753-9.
